title: Purely-logarithmic-time- and constant-space-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation
abstract: We prove that constant-space-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation can be achieved with provably strictly logarithmic time overhead, improving over the best known results with additional subpolylogarithmic factors. Our main construction uses polynomial-subrank transversal logical $\CCZ$ gates on good quantum locally testable codes to implement addressable universal computation by transferring batches of logical qubits between dense storage and active logical subspaces while reusing the same ancillary workspace. Logical $\CCZ$ gates are implemented directly by the transversal operation, so only stabilizer resource states require separate preparation. Furthermore, we give an alternative construction that also achieves purely logarithmic time overhead based on modifying the quantum Reed--Solomon magic-state distillation scheme of Nguyen and Pattison. Recursively applying a fixed distillation circuit protected by qLTCs of increasing block length eliminates the subpolylogarithmic time factor.
summary: This paper presents a significant theoretical advancement in fault-tolerant quantum computation, proving that universal computation can be achieved with purely logarithmic time overhead and constant space overhead. The authors achieve this using advanced techniques involving transversal logical gates on locally testable codes. This result significantly improves upon previous state-of-the-art bounds for building scalable quantum computers.
main_problem: The paper aims to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computation with the optimal overheads of purely logarithmic time and constant space overhead.
main_result: It proves that such computation is possible using transversal logical CCZ gates on good quantum locally testable codes, achieving a strictly logarithmic time overhead.
method: The construction involves transferring logical qubits between dense storage and active subspaces while reusing ancillary workspace, or alternatively, modifying quantum Reed-Solomon magic-state distillation.
model_or_system: The model is an adaptive Clifford+CCZ quantum circuit operating under a fault-tolerance framework using CSS codes, specifically $\Delta$-qLDPC and $(ho, \Delta)$-qLTCs.
key_observables: The primary observables are the time and space overheads required to simulate the ideal logical gate operations.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the target error $\epsilon$, the circuit width $W$, and the circuit depth $D$. The time overhead is $O(D \log(WD/\epsilon))$ and the space overhead is constant.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on the fault path avoiding specific 'bad' families of errors, and the analysis is conditional on the existence of certain positive constants.
paper_structure: The paper develops a rigorous framework by first establishing fault-tolerance using weight enumerators to constrain bad fault paths, then details the main construction using transversal CCZ gates for state transfer, and finally presents an alternative scheme via recursive distillation.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, optimized theoretical bounds on the resource overheads (time/space) for universal quantum computation, which is foundational knowledge for designing practical quantum hardware architectures.
